title: Acceptance for fragmented outputs and tool degradation playbook
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem summary: Customer workloads are increasingly relying on mixed synchronous and asynchronous tool invocations from streamed model output. Current acceptance artifacts focus on full-message contracts; we need a single, operational acceptance spec that covers fragmented (partial) emissions, deterministic stitch points, error taxonomy for tool degradation, and an operator playbook for reconciliation and remediation.

Goal: Define acceptance criteria and testable requirements so that product, engineering, and SRE teams can ship a runtime + console behavior that: (1) guarantees deterministic envelope sequencing for fragments, (2) surfaces clear fault classes when downstream tools fail or degrade, (3) provides a reconcilable audit trail for partial outputs and replay, and (4) documents operator runbooks and user-facing fallbacks for production incidents.

Scope: Applies to hosted API and Dedicated deployments for text/chat streaming and function/tool calling. This PRD covers contract (schema), streaming boundaries, idempotency on retried tool calls, telemetry/observability signals needed for acceptance, and an operator playbook for degraded tool availability. Exclusions: deep internal kernel selection optimizations and model training changes are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic fragment envelope format: every streamed fragment must include a monotonically increasing 'fragment_index' and a stable 'response_envelope_id' for the overall output; acceptance tests validate ordering and detect missing fragments within a 3-second grace window.

Partial-object semantics: fragments that represent partial JSON object fields must include an explicit 'stitch_point' token and a final 'fragment_final=true' emission; consumer SDKs can reconstruct the object without heuristic parsing in >=95% of canonical test prompts.

Tool call idempotency: any tool invocation emitted by the model runtime must include a unique 'tool_call_id' computed by the gateway; retries are allowed only when the tool response indicates a transient error class (see error taxonomy) and must not exceed 3 retries by default; acceptance tests verify no duplicate side-effects for idempotent-designated tool APIs in 1000 simulated requests.

Graceful degradation modes: define three modes when a bound tool degrades: soft-fail (model emits a fallback value and continues), stubbed-response (synthetic deterministic stub), and circuit-open (stop further tool calls and emit a clear error fragment). Each mode must be selectable per-route and passing tests must demonstrate all three modes for a sample tool integration.

Observable signals: runtime must emit structured events to the telemetry pipeline for fragment-emitted, fragment-finalized, tool-call-start, tool-call-end, tool-call-error (with class), and reconcile-start/reconcile-end. Each event must contain response_envelope_id and tool_call_id for correlation.

Operator playbook: console must surface a per-envelope timeline with fragment events and tool-call statuses; on detected missing fragments past the grace window, operator can trigger auto-replay, manual replay, or mark as irreparable. Acceptance includes a console UI checklist and test run-through recorded in the staging environment.

Backward-compatibility: legacy clients that do not send 'accepts_fragments=true' header must continue to receive a best-effort single-message assembly for at least 6 months after rollout; acceptance tests include compatibility scenarios with older SDKs.
Security/control gates: private deployments must respect KMS/HSM for any persisted tool-call payloads and audit logs; acceptance requires a security checklist sign-off for the feature before GA.
test_cases: Unit tests: envelope ID and fragment_index monotonicity under concurrent streaming producers (load test: 500 concurrent streams) must pass.
Integration tests: simulate a tool returning intermittent 503s and validate runtime triggers fallback stub mode and emits tool-call-error events with correct error_class field.
Chaos test: introduce delayed fragments and validate console shows missing-fragment alert and operator-initiated replay succeeds in >=90% of runs.

End-to-end: sample customer prompt that triggers three tool calls in a single stream; tests verify correct ordering, no duplicate tool side-effects, and full reconstructability of the final JSON object.
Compatibility regression: older SDK requests without fragment headers receive assembled response within 2s additional latency budget.
decision_notes: Tradeoff: requiring fragment_final marker simplifies reconstruction for downstream consumers but increases surface area of the model-output contract; engineering prefers optional finalization to reduce model prompts; PM opts for explicit final flag to meet reliability SLAs.
Decision: default retry policy set to 3 retries with exponential backoff; operator-configurable per-route policies will be added in a follow-up (see dependencies).
Tradeoff: expose three degradation modes to customers for flexibility; increased complexity in Console UX accepted because observability gains are high.

operator_playbook: Detection: Console alerts on missing fragments after 3s grace window and marks envelope as 'incomplete'.
Triage: operator reviews fragment timeline and tool-call events; if tool-call-error shows class 'transient', trigger auto-replay; if 'permanent', switch route to stubbed-response.
Remediation: manual replay invokes reconcile API with response_envelope_id; if replay fails, mark incident and notify customer-facing team.
Escalation: if >5% envelopes show incomplete state for a route in 30m, open Incident with SRE and Product; priority P0 if user-visible error rate >2%.
Postmortem: include fragment and tool-call events in incident report; attach console timeline and replay logs.
implementation_tips: Use a compact wire format for fragment headers to avoid token bloat (e.g., short keys like fi, re_id, tf), documented in the API reference.
Add SDK helpers for reassembly to reduce client-side parsing bugs; include a deterministic algorithm for stitch points in the SDKs.
Provide a local 'dry-run' mode for partner integrations to validate idempotency without producing side-effects (sandbox mode).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased telemetry costs from high-volume fragment events. Mitigation: sampling and aggregated rollups for low-priority routes.
Risk: customer SDK fragmentation; Mitigation: ship SDK helpers and a canonical reassembler across languages.
Risk: downstream tool non-idempotency causing duplicate side-effects on retries. Mitigation: require partner integrations to declare idempotent-safe endpoints and support sandbox verification.
